title: Teams-to-AD CS intrusions - KB AppData runtime execution
subtitle: Defender XDR hunt for source-observed Bun or Java execution from KB-prefixed AppData Roaming paths
decision: Publish as a campaign-scoped hunting query, not an alert. Investigate matches as portable-runtime execution leads and require independent Teams, remote-support, discovery, identity or certificate evidence before associating a result with either documented intrusion.
key_findings: Microsoft investigated two human-operated intrusions that began with Teams help-desk impersonation and remote access, then staged portable runtimes and assessed AD CS. [C001]

The reusable endpoint observable is Bun or Java executing a script from a KB-prefixed AppData Roaming directory; one variant used a renamed Bun binary whose version metadata retained the original filename. [C002]
Microsoft published the exact DeviceProcessEvents conditions implemented here and explicitly positioned them as an investigation starting point requiring tenant validation and correlation. [C003]
source_facts: The source documents archive placement during a remote session, extraction into a newly created user-profile directory, portable runtime execution and subsequent discovery or AD CS assessment. [C001]
The source-published hunt filters Bun or Java process identity, a .js or .java command-line operand, and a numeric KB-prefixed AppData Roaming execution path. [C002][C003]
DeviceProcessEvents and every field used by the query are documented in the Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting schema. [C004]
analyst_assessment: The combined runtime, script operand and path constraints are materially more specific than a runtime name or user-writable path alone, but the KB path is campaign-scoped and mutable. [C005]

A match establishes only that the recorded process event met the published endpoint conditions; it does not establish Teams contact, remote-control success, AD CS abuse or certificate issuance. [C005]
T1059.007 applies to the Bun JavaScript branch and T1036 applies to the source-observed renamed runtime and update-themed staging context. [C006]
assumptions: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint populates full FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine and process version metadata across the intended Windows device scope. [C004]
Authorized software deployment and developer workflows can be resolved to durable owners during triage. [C007]
unknowns: Microsoft did not disclose campaign dates, actor attribution or the exact prevalence of each runtime variant.
Target-environment benign prevalence and ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName population are not measured.
The endpoint event alone cannot establish the preceding Teams interaction or subsequent AD CS activity.
technical_background: In two investigated intrusions, Microsoft observed help-desk impersonation through Teams followed by user-approved remote access. The operator placed an archive, extracted it under a newly created user-profile directory and launched attacker-controlled code with portable Python, Bun or Java runtimes before host discovery and AD CS assessment. Runtime choice varied, so this package retains only the source-published Bun/Java process observable: an executable identified by filename or Bun original-file metadata, a JavaScript or Java source operand and a KB-prefixed directory under AppData Roaming. [C001][C002][C003]

attack_chain.behavior: External Teams messages or calls impersonate support personnel and persuade a user to start remote control.
attack_chain.observable: Teams interaction and approved remote-support evidence; not queried by this package.

attack_chain.behavior: An archive is transferred and extracted into a newly created KB-prefixed directory under the user profile.
attack_chain.observable: User-writable AppData Roaming path and surrounding file/process timeline.

attack_chain.behavior: Bun or Java executes attacker-controlled JavaScript or Java source from the staged directory.
attack_chain.observable: DeviceProcessEvents with runtime identity, script operand and KB-prefixed FolderPath.

attack_chain.behavior: The staged components perform discovery and assess AD CS before the intrusion diverges into ESC1 or ESC8 paths.
attack_chain.observable: Discovery process lineage, LDAPS/SMB activity, Defender alerts, CA records and Kerberos evidence; enrichment only.

telemetry.purpose: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process-creation records for the source-published hunt.

telemetry.field: Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine
telemetry.purpose: Time scope, stable device pivot, runtime identity, execution location and script operand.
Identify renamed Bun, preserve file/process context and support event-level investigation.
Preserve parent and user context for ownership and timeline analysis.

telemetry.field: CloudAppEvents, AlertInfo, AlertEvidence, CA/IIS and Kerberos records
telemetry.purpose: Test the non-claim boundary by corroborating Teams, relay, certificate and authentication activity.

query.logic: Return Bun or Java process events from numeric KB-prefixed AppData Roaming directories when the command line references JavaScript or Java source.
query.match_proves: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint recorded a process event matching the published runtime identity, script operand and KB-prefixed AppData path conditions.
query.match_does_not_prove: Teams impersonation, unauthorized remote access, malicious script content, AD CS assessment, ESC1 or ESC8 abuse, certificate issuance, PKINIT, DCSync, exfiltration or attribution.

triage: Preserve the raw DeviceProcessEvents row, query version, Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ProcessUniqueId and ReportId.
Confirm that FolderPath is the runtime image location and inspect ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName, FileName, SHA1 and file provenance without treating version metadata as signature evidence.
Recover the complete ProcessCommandLine and inspect the referenced .js or .java file, archive origin and creation timeline using authorized endpoint evidence.
Determine whether the runtime, KB-prefixed directory and account belong to approved software deployment, development or support activity.
Pivot to the initiating process and surrounding process/network timeline for discovery commands and LDAPS or SMB connections.
Escalate campaign linkage only when independent Teams, remote-support, Defender alert, CA issuance or Kerberos evidence corroborates the endpoint match.

false_positives.source: Approved portable Java or Bun deployment in a KB-named application directory
false_positives.control: Require package provenance, software owner, deployment record and expected script path or hash.

false_positives.source: Developer or QA execution of JavaScript or Java source from a user-writable test directory
false_positives.control: Validate device role, user role, repository origin and repeatable development workflow.

false_positives.source: Version metadata or command-line field gaps
false_positives.control: Retain raw events and reject promotion if required branches cannot be evaluated consistently.

steps: Confirm DeviceProcessEvents coverage and population of every queried and projected field on representative Windows devices.
In an authorized lab, run a benign portable Bun or Java runtime from AppData\Roaming\KB12345 with a harmless .js or .java operand and retain the raw process event.
Run negative controls: the same runtime outside a KB-prefixed path, the KB path without a .js/.java operand, and an unrelated executable inside the KB path.
Execute the query unchanged and verify that the controlled positive is returned while all three negative controls are excluded.
Measure at least 30 days of historical prevalence, resolve every owner and document any legitimate software families before considering alert logic.
validation.success: The controlled positive returns one complete, explainable row; required fields are populated; negative controls do not match; and benign historical results can be separated with durable provenance.
validation.rejection: Reject promotion when FolderPath or ProcessCommandLine is absent, process version metadata is unreliable for the Bun branch, negative controls match, or benign ownership remains unbounded.
visibility_gaps: No direct visibility into Teams interaction from this query
No proof of script contents or malicious intent
No CA issuance, PKINIT or DCSync evidence
Mutable folder name and runtime choice
validation.promotion_gate: Require retained positive and negative controls, field-completeness evidence, measured prevalence, durable allowlisting and an accountable owner before designing alert logic.

conclusion: The source-published process pattern is specific enough for a Defender XDR hunt and distinct from existing repository coverage, but it remains campaign-scoped and untested. Treat matches as endpoint execution leads; do not infer Teams delivery or AD CS compromise without independent evidence.
